unit.title: Introductions and the correct form
unit.needIt: Knowing how to introduce people helps you avoid awkward silences and makes others feel respected. It helps you navigate job interviews and social parties without feeling nervous.
unit.why: Imagine you are at a party and see a friend standing alone with a stranger. If you jump in and introduce them correctly, you make your friend feel included and the stranger feel welcomed. It turns a lonely moment into a comfortable conversation.
unit.outcome: Navigate social introductions with confidence and grace.
unit.reachesYou: You meet this when meeting a new coworker at a desk or meeting your friend's parents for the first time. It happens every time you are the bridge between two people who do not know each other.
unit.do: Next time you are with a friend and meet someone new, introduce your friend first by saying their name clearly.

quiz.q: Which word is better for formal occasions?
quiz.why: The text states that 'present' is the preferred word for formal events.
quiz.quote: The word "present" is preferable on formal occasions to the word "introduce."

quiz.q: Who should be presented to whom in a formal setting?
quiz.why: The text says a gentleman is always presented to a lady regardless of age.
quiz.quote: The younger person is always presented to the older or more distinguished, but a gentleman is always presented to a lady, even though he is an old gentleman of great distinction and the lady a mere slip of a girl.

quiz.q: How should you introduce a person of high rank like a Cardinal?
quiz.why: Doctors, judges, and bishops are introduced by their titles.
quiz.quote: A doctor, a judge, a bishop, are addressed and introduced by their titles.

quiz.q: When introducing two ladies to each other, what is the rule?
choices: The younger lady is always first
The married lady is always first
The lady with the higher rank is first
quiz.why: The text states that in introducing two ladies to each other or one gentleman to another, no distinction is made.
quiz.quote: As a matter of fact, in introducing two ladies to each other or one gentleman to another, no distinction is made.

quiz.q: What is the rule for introducing a daughter to a married lady?
quiz.why: The text says it is bad taste to call a daughter 'Miss Mary' to anyone but a servant.
quiz.quote: The daughter's name is omitted because it is ’ extremely bad taste (except in the South) to call her daughter y"Miss Mary" to any one but a servant

quiz.why: The text explicitly says asking 'What is your name?' is abrupt.
quiz.quote: Most people of good taste very much dislike being asked their names. To say "What is your name?" is always abrupt and unflattering.

quiz.why: The text says asking 'What is your name?' is too direct and rude.
quiz.quote: To say "What is your name?" is always abrupt and unflattering.

partials: Introduce the younger to the older.
A gentleman is presented to a lady.

crystal.key: Manners of introduction focus on showing respect through proper order and titles.

decoys.text: Always ask for a person's name.
decoys.why: The text says asking 'What is your name?' is abrupt and unflattering.

decoys.text: Introduce people by their first names only.
decoys.why: The text says doctors, judges, and bishops should be introduced by their titles.

crystal.aha: By following the correct order and using proper titles, you remove social friction and make others feel comfortable.

beats.say: A good introduction is a bridge for others.
